cards.text: It's the same day Jesus rose, and the two who walked to Emmaus are back in Jerusalem with the Eleven, Jesus' closest disciples, and those with them. They're telling everyone how they recognized Jesus when He broke the bread. And while they're still describing it, Jesus Himself is standing right there among them.

cards.question: Jesus is suddenly standing in the middle of the room. What are the first words He says to them?
The second Jesus shows up, the whole room bursts into cheers.
The disciples are startled and frightened. They think they've seen a ___.

cards.text: Jesus asks them why they're troubled and why doubts are rising in their hearts. Honestly, friend? I'd have been right there with them, hiding behind my own mustache like it was a curtain.

cards.question: To show them it's really Him, Jesus tells the disciples to look at His ___ and His ___.
While He's proving it's really Him, Jesus tells the disciples not to touch Him.

cards.text: He shows them His hands and feet. They STILL can't quite believe it, but now it's because of their joy and amazement.

cards.question: While the disciples are still taking it all in, Jesus asks them a question. What does He ask for?
What do the disciples hand Jesus?

cards.text: And He takes it and eats it right in front of them. Spirits don't snack, friend, and if they did, I'd have blamed them for every cookie that ever went missing from my jar.
Then Jesus reminds them of what He told them while He was still with them. Everything written about Him in the Scriptures must be fulfilled.

cards.question: Jesus names where those things about Him are written: the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the ___.
Next, Jesus opens something so the disciples can understand the Scriptures. What does He open?

cards.text: He tells them what's written: the Christ will suffer and rise from the dead on the third day. And there He is, friend, standing right in front of them.

cards.question: Jesus says something will be proclaimed in His name to all nations. What is it?

answers.text: A new law for every land

cards.question: That message about repentance and forgiveness goes out to all nations, beginning in ___.
Jesus tells the disciples to keep everything they've seen to themselves.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "And behold, I am sending the promise of My Father upon you." A promise from the Father beats anything I found in that junk drawer, friend, and I shared that drawer with an expired coupon that believed in itself HARD.

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples to wait until they've been clothed with power from on high. Where does He tell them to stay until then?

cards.text: Then Jesus leads them out as far as Bethany. He lifts up His hands and blesses them.

cards.question: While Jesus is still blessing the disciples at Bethany, what happens?

answers.text: He is carried up into heaven
He sends them out two by two
He breaks bread with them again

cards.text: They worship Him and head back to Jerusalem with great joy. From frightened to GREAT JOY, friend, that's a bigger turnaround than me going from the back of a junk drawer to a whole planet of my own!

cards.question: Back in Jerusalem, the disciples are praising God continually in the ___.

findings.problem: The opening card uses facts from outside the passage but cites only Luke 24:36. It says it is the same day Jesus rose, that the two from Emmaus are back in Jerusalem with the Eleven, and that they recognized Jesus when He broke the bread (Luke 24:13, 33, 35). None of these carry their reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to pick Jesus' exact first words ('Peace be with you') from other plausible greetings ('Do not be afraid', 'Grace be with you'). Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason it out, so it tests wording they haven't seen and comes down to luck. 'Do not be afraid' is also close enough in purpose that a baker could argue for it.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The fill-in-the-blank 'the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the ___' asks the baker to finish Jesus' wording in Luke 24:44. Card 1 only said 'the Scriptures', so the baker is guessing the next word of a line, not reasoning out meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The right answer 'In the city' is a generic phrase, while both wrong answers name a specific town ('In Emmaus', 'In Capernaum'). The right answer stands out as a different kind of answer. Naming the city (Jerusalem, as Luke 24:52 shows) or making all three answers the same kind would fix it.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
